capacity_gross_kwh.notes: Lexus USA: "The 71.4 kWh battery"; RZ 450e battery developed by PPES (2025 Lexus release).

capacity_usable_kwh.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists 71.4 kWh nominal / 64.0 kWh usable for the same-size 71.4 kWh bZ4X pack (European listing; Toyota/Lexus state total only). Lexus RZ 450e uses the 71.4 kWh pack (Lexus 2023 and 2025 pressroom pages).

chemistry.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists NMC for the 71.4 kWh bZ4X pack; the RZ 450e uses the same 71.4 kWh pack (Lexus 2023/2025 pressroom pages). Compared 2023-2025: no pack change described.

nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: EV Database lists 355 V for the 71.4 kWh bZ4X pack; the RZ 450e uses the same pack (Lexus 2023 pressroom).

preconditioning.notes: Estimated: Motor1 says the 2026 RZ "gains" an upgraded charging system with preconditioning, i.e. the 2023-2025 cars lacked it; Lexus 2023-2025 pages describe DC charging with no battery-warming feature; EV Database lists preconditioning "No" for the 71.4 kWh bZ4X sibling. Compared 2023, 2024 and 2025 pages: no change described.

ac_max_kw.notes: Lexus USA 2026 release: the 11 kW charger is "up from 7-kW capacity on the prior model year", i.e. 7 kW on 2025 and earlier.

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: InsideEVs test of the bZ4X: the 71.4 kWh PPES pack (US bZ4X FWD, single motor) charges at up to 150 kW; the RZ 450e uses the same pack but has two motors, so this is a weak basis. Lexus pages for 2023-2025 give times only (low battery light to 80% in about 30 min), no peak kW. A Lexus RZ charging-information page and EV Database (unopenable: 403 and 429) reportedly give 150 kW and 147 kW.
